name: Calm's Undead/Demon trigger is native DBC data, not a missing script (#442)
contract: Spell.dbc 804057 ("Calm", SpellFamilyName 33) effect 0 is SPELL_EFFECT_TRIGGER_SPELL (64) with EffectTriggerSpell 807778 and implicit target 6 (the spell's own enemy target); Spell::EffectTriggerSpell's 'normal case' branch (SpellEffects.cpp:1204-1245, since 807778 is not one of the hardcoded special-case ids above it) casts 807778 on that same unitTarget unconditionally via m_caster->CastSpell(...). 807778 ("Calm - Undead/Demon Trigger") carries the DBC-level TargetCreatureType field set to 36 = (1<<2)|(1<<5), the bitmask for CREATURE_TYPE_DEMON(3) and CREATURE_TYPE_UNDEAD(6); SpellInfo::CheckTarget calls CheckTargetCreatureType (SpellInfo.cpp:1974,2060-2072), which Spell::AddUnitTarget invokes for every candidate target during normal target selection (Spell.cpp:2350-2364) — including this triggered cast. So 807778's own two aura effects (SPELL_AURA_MOD_PACIFY=25 and SPELL_AURA_MOD_ROOT=26, i.e. "unable to attack or move") are added only when the target's creature type overlaps that mask, and silently dropped for every other target: a fully native, DBC-driven gate with zero server script involved. The disarm portion (effects 1/2 of 804057 itself, SPELL_AURA_MOD_DISARM=67 and SPELL_AURA_MOD_DISARM_OFFHAND=254) is unconditional and already known to work per the issue report. This scenario proves the creature-type gate: 807778 lands on an Undead target and does not land on a Humanoid one. Calm and its trigger both roll spell hit against the same-level targets, so a miss left the disarm or the trigger absent; both casters carry spell_hit_rating.

steps.label: Let spawn AI and level scaling settle
Disarm still applies to the Undead target (unconditional effect)
Undead/Demon trigger 807778 lands on an Undead target
Disarm still applies to the Humanoid target (unconditional effect)
Wait through the trigger's cast window before asserting absence
Undead/Demon trigger 807778 does not land on a Humanoid target
